An OBD GPS tracker is a vehicle tracking device that plugs directly into your car's OBD-II diagnostic port, usually located under the dashboard near the steering wheel.

What can it do?

Real-time GPS tracking: Monitor your vehicle's location through an app or website.

Trip history: Review routes, mileage, and driving activity.

Geofencing: Receive alerts when a vehicle enters or leaves a designated area.

Driving behavior: Monitor speeding, harsh braking, and acceleration.

Vehicle diagnostics: Some models read fault codes and vehicle health information.

Easy installation: Plug-and-play, generally without wiring.

Most real-time trackers require a cellular connection and a monthly subscription.
